title: structured output: improve constrained-decoding backends (CFG / regex / tokenizer edgecases)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improved structured-output constrained decoding: added CFG and regex backends, tokenizer alignment fixes for regex/grammar constraints, incremental streaming-safe constraint checking. Backwards compatible; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: customers rely on structured-output (function/tool calling and schema-constrained responses). We continue to see two classes of failures in production and tests: (1) grammar/CFG constraints that require a different evaluation model than simple prefix regex, and (2) regex/constraint mismatches caused by tokenizer/BPE boundaries which result in invalid or partially-matched tokens during streaming. This PR refactors the constrained-decoding plumbing into a backend abstraction and ships two production-ready backends (CFG and regex) plus tokenizer-edgecase fixes.

What changed (high-level): extracted a ConstrainedDecodingBackend trait that supports incremental state, lookahead, and rollback; added cfg_backend (Earley-derived incremental matcher optimized for common Redwood schemas), added regex_backend with tokenizer-aware alignment and optional byte-level fallback; implemented tokenizer/regex alignment helpers to ensure constraint matching respects token boundaries; streaming path updated to use incremental constraint checks and buffered emission to avoid emitting invalid partial tokens; function-calling/OpenAI-compatible structured output flow preserved by mapping backend remainders to function arguments in the same shape as before.

Testing and validation: added comprehensive unit tests for both backends (including fuzz tests for tokenizer edgecases), end-to-end streaming integration tests that exercise chunked emission + constraint enforcement, and a small perf benchmark suite. Benchmarks on a c6g-like instance (representative dev rig) show ~6-9% overhead for strict CFG checks at 2048 context but near-zero overhead for typical regex constraints; memory overhead <1.5MB per request in worst-case CFG scenarios.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind a feature flag structured_output.constrained_decoding_backend with default enabled for hosted integration tests. Will flip flag for Canary customers after 48h of post-merge telemetry review.

Related: ENG-7931 (schema-driven constrained decoding), ENG-8056 (streaming stability), ENG-8094 (tokenizer edgecases).

Implement cfg_backend with incremental parser and optimizations for common schema shapes
Implement regex_backend with tokenizer-aligned matching and byte-level fallback
Tokenizer: add regex alignment utilities and unit tests for BPE boundary cases
Streaming: integrate incremental constraint checks and buffered emission path
Add unit, integration, and fuzz tests for tokenizer edgecases
Docs: update structured-output README and add migration notes
Fix: small lock contention issue in backend state (perf tweak)

discussion_summary: This PR refactors the constrained-decoding implementation into an extensible backend model and ships CFG and regex backends that address longstanding tokenizer boundary and streaming emission issues. Review focused on perf, thread-safety, and test coverage; all concerns were addressed. Backwards compatibility preserved and rollout controlled via feature flag.
